title: For a closed immersion i with ideal J, the unit F -> i_* i^* F is the quotient F -> F/JF
statement: Let $i:Z\to Y$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion] with ideal sheaf $\mathcal J=\ker(\mathcal O_Y\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and let $i^*\dashv i_*$ be the pullback and pushforward of modules [def-pc-module-pullback], with unit $\eta_{\mathcal F}:\mathcal F\to i_*i^*\mathcal F$. For an $\mathcal O_Y$-module $\mathcal F$ let $\mathcal J\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal F$ be the image of the multiplication map $\mathcal J\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] (the subsheaf generated by the local products $as$). Then for every $\mathcal O_Y$-module $\mathcal F$ the map $\eta_{\mathcal F}$ is surjective (as a map of sheaves) with kernel $\mathcal J\mathcal F$; hence it induces an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules $\bar\eta_{\mathcal F}:\mathcal F/\mathcal J\mathcal F\to i_*i^*\mathcal F$ (the source the cokernel of $\mathcal J\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$), natural in $\mathcal F$.

source.place: Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma 04CJ (spaces-morphisms-lemma-i-star-equivalence) part (1), stated for closed immersions of algebraic spaces, of which a closed immersion of schemes is the special case; the stalkwise argument is that of the proof of Modules, Lemma 08KS (modules-lemma-i-star-equivalence), literature/stacks-project/modules.tex: at x not in i(Z) both F_x/(JF)_x and (i_*i^*F)_x vanish (J_x = O_{Y,x}), at x = i(z) the stalk map is F_x -> F_x (x)_{O_{Y,x}} O_{Y,x}/J_x (Sheaves 0098, 00AE)

proof.text: The unit $\eta_{\mathcal F}:\mathcal F\to i_*i^*\mathcal F$ is a morphism of \mathcal O_Y-modules by the adjunction in [def-pc-module-pullback]. To identify its kernel and image it is enough to compute its stalk maps and then use the stalkwise criteria for sheaf maps.

source.place: Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma 04CJ, with the sheaf-theoretic stalk criteria used in the proof of Modules, Lemma 08KS

proof.text: Let $x\in Y\setminus i(Z)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks](1), $(i_*i^*\mathcal F)_x=0$. Since $i(Z)$ is closed, choose an open neighbourhood $V$ of $x$ disjoint from $i(Z)$. The kernel definition of $\mathcal J$ in [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] gives $\mathcal J(V)=\mathcal O_Y(V)$, so $1\in\mathcal J(V)$ and every germ of $\mathcal F$ at $x$ lies in $(\mathcal J\mathcal F)_x$. Thus the stalk of $\eta_{\mathcal F}$ is the zero map with kernel $(\mathcal J\mathcal F)_x$ and is surjective.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 08KS, proof of the case outside the closed subset; the pushforward stalk calculation is Sheaves, Lemma 00AE

proof.text: Now let $z\in Z$ and $x=i(z)$. Write $R=\mathcal O_{Y,x}$, $S=\mathcal O_{Z,z}$, and let $\varphi:R\to S$ be the local-ring map induced by $i$. The sheaf map $\mathcal O_Y\to i_*\mathcal O_Z$ is surjective for a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks](2) identifies its target stalk with $S$. Hence $\varphi$ is surjective. Its kernel is the stalk $K=\mathcal J_x$: taking stalks preserves the kernel in the definition of $\mathcal J$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf].

source.place: Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma 04CJ; the local-ring description is the stalkwise argument of Modules, Lemma 08KS

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-pullback], $(i^*\mathcal F)_z$ is naturally $\mathcal F_x\otimes_R S$, and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks](2) identifies $(i_*i^*\mathcal F)_x$ with this tensor product. Under these identifications the stalk of the adjunction unit sends $m\in\mathcal F_x$ to $m\otimes1$: this is exactly the germ description of the pullback unit in [def-pc-module-pullback].

source.place: Modules, Lemma 08KS, proof at a point of the closed subscheme, using Sheaves, Lemmas 0098 and 00AE

proof.text: For a surjective ring map $R\to S$ with kernel $K$ and an $R$-module $M$, the canonical map $M\to M\otimes_R S$, $m\mapsto m\otimes1$, is surjective with kernel $KM$: identify $S$ with $R/K$, use the relations $m\otimes\bar r=rm\otimes1$, and define the inverse of $M/KM\to M\otimes_RR/K$ by $m\otimes\bar r\mapsto rm+KM$. Applying this with $M=\mathcal F_x$ and $K=\mathcal J_x$, and observing from the image definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] that $(\mathcal J\mathcal F)_x=\mathcal J_x\mathcal F_x$, shows that the stalk of $\eta_{\mathcal F}$ at $x$ is surjective with kernel $(\mathcal J\mathcal F)_x$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 08KS, proof of the local algebra fact $G_x\to G_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\mathcal O_{Z,z}$

proof.text: The two cases cover every point of $Y$, so [lem-weil-pbc-locally-surjective-iff-stalks] makes $\eta_{\mathcal F}$ a surjective sheaf morphism, and the stalk computation identifies its kernel with $\mathcal J\mathcal F$. The sheaf first-isomorphism theorem therefore gives the induced map $\bar\eta_{\mathcal F}:\mathcal F/\mathcal J\mathcal F\to i_*i^*\mathcal F$. Its stalk maps are the isomorphisms $\mathcal F_x/\mathcal J_x\mathcal F_x\cong\mathcal F_x\otimes_R S$ from the preceding algebra calculation, so [lem-weil-pbc-module-iso-on-stalks] makes $\bar\eta_{\mathcal F}$ an isomorphism. All constructions are induced by the natural adjunction unit and multiplication, hence the isomorphism is natural in $\mathcal F$.

source.place: Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma 04CJ (1), with the stalkwise proof of Modules, Lemma 08KS and naturality of the adjunction unit

split_report.summary: Split the unit-to-quotient statement along Morphisms 04CJ and the stalkwise proof of Modules 08KS. The six steps handle the stalk outside the closed image, the surjective local-ring map and its ideal kernel at a point of the closed subscheme, the pullback stalk and unit germ, the elementary tensor-with-a-quotient calculation, and the global surjectivity, kernel and natural isomorphism. No new DAG nodes were needed: all non-elementary ingredients are existing cited nodes.
